import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive visualization
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 12))

# Set style
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# 1. Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type (scatter plot)
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
sensor_types = df['sensor_type'].unique()
colors = sns.color_palette("husl", len(sensor_types))
for i, sensor in enumerate(sensor_types):
    subset = df[df['sensor_type'] == sensor]
    ax1.scatter(subset['megapixels'], subset['price_usd'], 
                alpha=0.6, label=sensor, c=[colors[i]], s=30)
ax1.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_title('Camera Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.legend(title='Sensor Type', loc='upper left', fontsize=9)

# 2. Average Price by Brand (top 10 brands by count)
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
top_brands = df['brand'].value_counts().head(10).index
brand_prices = df[df['brand'].isin(top_brands)].groupby('brand')['price_usd'].mean().sort_values(ascending=True)
bars = ax2.barh(brand_prices.index, brand_prices.values, color=sns.color_palette("viridis", len(brand_prices)))
ax2.set_xlabel('Average Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_ylabel('Brand', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_title('Average Camera Price by Brand (Top 10)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
for i, v in enumerate(brand_prices.values):
    ax2.text(v + 50, i, f'${v:.0f}', va='center', fontsize=9)

# 3. Distribution of Body Types with 4K Video capability
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
body_4k = df.groupby(['body_type', 'has_video_4k']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
body_4k.columns = ['No 4K', 'Has 4K']
body_4k.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax3, color=['#ff7f0e', '#1f77b4'], edgecolor='black', width=0.7)
ax3.set_xlabel('Body Type', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_ylabel('Number of Cameras', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_title('Camera Body Types and 4K Video Capability', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.legend(title='4K Video', fontsize=9)
ax3.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 4. Evolution of Megapixels over Model Years
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
yearly_stats = df.groupby('model_year').agg({
    'megapixels': ['mean', 'std'],
    'price_usd': 'mean'
}).reset_index()
yearly_stats.columns = ['model_year', 'mp_mean', 'mp_std', 'price_mean']

ax4.fill_between(yearly_stats['model_year'], 
                  yearly_stats['mp_mean'] - yearly_stats['mp_std'],
                  yearly_stats['mp_mean'] + yearly_stats['mp_std'],
                  alpha=0.3, color='steelblue', label='Std Dev')
ax4.plot(yearly_stats['model_year'], yearly_stats['mp_mean'], 
         color='steelblue', linewidth=2, marker='o', markersize=5, label='Mean Megapixels')
ax4.set_xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_ylabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_title('Evolution of Camera Megapixels Over Time', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.legend(loc='upper left', fontsize=9)

# Adjust layout
plt.suptitle('Digital Camera Market Analysis (1000 Cameras)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
